text: In the year 1962 the main Icelandic newspaper, Morgunblaðið (the Morning Paper), announced that part of the treasure known popularly as Egils Silver had been found: In the twilight on Friday, a man from Mosfell County found part of the silver of Egil Skallagrimsson in the so-called Kýrgil (Cow Ravine) that comes out of the mountain of Mosfell, close to the farm Minna-Mosfell. The farmer, Guðmundur Ásmundsson, was giving his horses water when a part of the bank fell out from under his horses hoof and something clattered against the horseshoe. The farmer looked closely and discovered ancient silver money. Yesterday morning when he was digging at that same place, he found 30 silver coins. The news about the treasure drew nation-wide interest and curious newspaper readers rushed out to Mosfell in order to get a peek at or even uncover some more of the silver. However, they found nothing, and when they reread that mornings paper, they noticed only then that it was April First, April Fools Day.
